other_failure_modes.name: target_encoding_self_leakage
other_failure_modes.description: When computing target encodings within cross-validation folds, the agent maps the fold's aggregated target statistics back to the training indices without using leave-one-out or out-of-fold techniques. This causes the training features to contain the target value of the row itself, leading to severe overfitting.

other_failure_modes.name: validation_leakage_imputation
other_failure_modes.description: Imputation statistics (e.g., median) are calculated on the entire training set before cross-validation splitting. This leaks information from the validation folds into the training folds.

summary: The agent develops a complex solution with extensive feature engineering, target encoding, and an ensemble of GBDTs and a PyTorch MLP. However, the solution suffers from critical data leakage: test data is leaked into training through global feature aggregations, and target encodings within the CV loop suffer from self-leakage because they map aggregate statistics directly back to the training rows without a leave-one-out strategy. Furthermore, random K-fold splitting is used on a temporal dataset, introducing look-ahead bias.
